body:
# the contributor audit of two newly closed proof routes

Neither result below is an OC counterexample. Both are exact auxiliary
counterexamples that prevent unsupported steps in a general proof.

## 1. Fixed-global-mass moment-body centroid

Source: `candidate 45e8a578c5c25d8d`.
Independent audit: `historical context (not an accepted premise)`.



The three homothetic triangles form their actual full-dimensional convex
hull with exactly three sampled fibers. Both endpoint masses are below
the prescribed t=M/2, so only the middle balanced moment body is feasible.
The top-cap exchange inequality, including the full-small-fiber endpoint,
gives a supporting line for each mass-dependent directional support
value. Homothetic cap inclusions give the stated correctly oriented
quantile bounds. Their sum is strictly increasing up to the maximum
common endpoint mass in every nonzero direction, because

    (225/256)^2 - 4(2559/131072)=45507/65536>0.

Thus equality with the fixed-mass Minkowski sum is an exact equality of
support functions. Its centroid is computed by a COMMON linear symmetry
group, not by an invalid assertion of centroid additivity under Minkowski
addition. The value is exactly

    (-1784/397827,-1784/397827).

the contributor separately derived the same cap area and exact positive deficit in
`candidate 1f389ff8934007f6`. The simpler integer
tilt in the final source also excludes/includes the endpoint triangles
strictly and has the same middle area. The prescribed centroid belongs
to the actual mixed set and to the cap; the failure is a depth failure.

No numerical claim is needed. The independent rational enclosure is
additional corroboration, not a premise of the symbolic argument.

## 2. Log-concavity and a greatest convex-order midpoint law

Source: `candidate 2439d77d03fde920`.



The explicit positive Hessian of u(x,t)=x^2/(2t)+t^3/6 has determinant
one. The displayed inverse map proves the exact convex image L=T(K),
and its area is 335/192. Convexity of K follows from the positive f''
on its entire possible x interval. Fenchel equality proves unique
quadratic-optimal coupling directly, without an unstated transport
uniqueness theorem. The midpoint density has log second derivative
1/81 at an interior point, so it is not log-concave even locally.

For Q=diag(1,2), the compact divergence-free variation preserves both
marginals. The integration-by-parts sign is correct:

    d/depsilon integral X^T Q T(psi_epsilon X) at zero
       = integral eta x/t^2 > 0.

Thus the Euclidean-quadratic optimizer cannot dominate all feasible laws
in convex order. Any putative greatest law would have to be that unique
optimizer, a contradiction. The actual three-fiber embedding keeps the
integer midpoint condition and positive fibers.

The same reasoning shows that starting from this optimizer, no feasible
convex-order dominating repair can be log-concave: its quadratic value
must already be maximal and uniqueness forces the identical law. This
does not affect the proved density-only selection theorem.

One exposition correction was requested: log-concavity alone would not
supply the exact finite-dimensional gamma_d constant in any case; its
centroid theorem supplies 1/e. The obstruction is failure of concavity,
not failure of smoothness, since this density is smooth near the test.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
